title: Health Cos Set Sights on 'Medical Geeks' for Leadership Roles

contentHtml:
Bengaluru: The transition among healthcare organisations from AI experimentation to enterprise-wide adoption has utnleashed a hunt for talent that can combine clinical expertise with engineering and AI skills.As healthcare companies look to build new capabilities, launch services and embed AI into product development and operations, search firms are seeing an uptick in mandates for chief business officers, heads of growth, as well as operations leaders and clinical and medical heads.

Compensation varies by role and company stage. Senior data, research and functional heads can earn ₹60 lakh to ₹1.5 crore, while CXO and business-head packages could reach ₹2-4 crore or more, with Esops often a significant add-on. Candidates with global experience and regulatory expertise can command a premium, and packages are increasingly linked to performance. Search firm Catenon saw a 30-40% increase in health-tech mandates.

Advt

"There is an uptick in hiring for senior roles in biostatistics, data analysis and research, with demand being driven by renewed investor confidence in the sector, a shift from growth-at-all-costs to evidence-led, profitable models, and the growing need for clinical-grade data and validated outcomes as AI-enabled products move into mainstream care," Gaurav Chattur, CEO of Catenon, told ET.

Overall, leadership hiring is concentrated where companies are scaling AI, expanding services and growing operations. Demand is strong for talent that can combine healthcare depth with the ability to responsibly scale AI-led products.

Executive search and talent advisory Longhouse is seeing health-tech mandates span the C-suite and functional leadership, not just technology.

"We are seeing AI-enabled healthcare as the most active segment, with senior moves across technology, commercial, people, legal and medical leadership, followed by digital health and diagnostics. Medtech, too, has been showing steady movement, mainly at CEO level and in growth and strategy roles," said Anshuman Das, CEO at Longhouse.Where roles need clinical, diagnostic or medtech depth, companies hire from within the sector: healthcare, health-tech, diagnostics, medtech, hospital and life sciences backgrounds. For functional roles, companies are open to leaders from sectors that have already scaled, said Das.

Advt

Companies are also hiring professionals from adjacent sectors such as enterprise technology, cloud, digital engineering and AI-driven organisations.Expat talent, too, is being tapped much of the time, with search firms saying companies are very open to overseas candidates. Returnees from the US, UK and Singapore are of particular interest, helped by India's growing ecosystem and the strength of its GCCs, Catenon's Chattur said.Digital healthcare platform MediBuddy is hiring across functions. It is looking to fill technology and product roles- including engineering, AI engineers, forward-deployed AI engineers who work directly alongside business teams and clients, product managers and programme managers. It is also looking for talent in healthcare delivery and customer experience.

Advt

"We are also hiring for growth-which covers business development, account management, category management and partnership teams, who work on both sides of our business," said Enbasekar Dinadayalane, co-founder of MediBuddy. Hiring is driven by the building of new capabilities and the launch of new healthcare services, as well as the embedding of AI across product development, engineering, and other functions.
